title: The Vibration Sensor That Invented a 300 Hz Tone
featured_title: THE VIBRATION SENSOR THAT INVENTED A 300 HZ TONE
subject: electrical-computer
audience: FE Electrical and Computer candidates and engineering students

presentation.challenge: The machine says 900 Hz. The sampled spectrum insists on 300 Hz.

practice.primary_question: Why can a 900 Hz analog tone appear as 300 Hz after sampling?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Reading an aliased FFT peak as a real analog frequency without checking fs/2.

case_dna.target_misconception: A sampled spectrum always reports the original analog frequency, even when the input exceeds the Nyquist limit.
case_dna.why_plausible: The ADC still produces a clean-looking sequence, so the lower-frequency alias can look like a real physical tone.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: A 900 Hz sinusoid sampled at 1200 samples/s exceeds the 600 Hz Nyquist frequency and aliases to |900 - 1200| = 300 Hz.
case_dna.corrected_model: Check the Nyquist condition before interpreting a sampled spectrum. Frequencies above fs/2 fold into baseband; increase sample rate or band-limit the input before sampling.

problem_statement: A vibration sensor carries a 900 Hz sinusoidal component into an ADC sampling at 1200 samples/s. The FFT shows a strong 300 Hz tone, and a review note labels it a real machine subharmonic. Diagnose the frequency shift, calculate the alias, and choose a sampling change that preserves the 900 Hz component without aliasing.
fixed_constraints: The signal of interest must be preserved

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The machine vibrates at 900 Hz. The data says 300 Hz.
gates.prompt: What sampling assumption failed before the FFT was interpreted?

options.label: The 900 Hz component aliases because it is above fs/2
options.reason: With fs = 1200 Hz, Nyquist is 600 Hz. The 900 Hz component folds to 300 Hz.

options.label: The FFT algorithm subtracts 600 Hz from every tone
options.reason: The ambiguity comes from undersampling, not an arbitrary FFT subtraction.

options.label: The sensor physically changed the vibration from 900 Hz to 300 Hz
options.reason: The stated analog input is 900 Hz; sampling explains the observed 300 Hz.

options.label: A large signal amplitude creates a one-third-frequency component
options.reason: Amplitude alone does not create this deterministic frequency fold.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the aliased frequency
gates.prompt: For a 900 Hz tone sampled at 1200 samples/s, what baseband frequency (Hz) will appear?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Sample the 900 Hz tone
gates.result: The sampled sequence produces a 300 Hz spectral peak even though the analog tone is 900 Hz.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Calculate the alias
gates.prompt: Use f_alias = |f - k fs| with k = 1. Enter |900 - 1200| in Hz.
gates.success: The alias is 300 Hz. The 900 Hz input exceeds the 600 Hz Nyquist limit.
gates.hint: Choose the multiple of fs that places the result between 0 and fs/2.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The sampling limits explain the false tone

cards.text: fs = 1200 samples/s gives a Nyquist frequency of 600 Hz.
The 900 Hz input is above Nyquist.
|900 - 1200| = 300 Hz, matching the observed FFT peak.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the spectrum review
report: C1. The analog vibration contains a 900 Hz component.
C2. The ADC samples at 1200 samples/s.
C3. The 300 Hz FFT peak proves a separate 300 Hz mechanical vibration exists.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: C2 is the stated sample rate.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: C3 ignores aliasing; the sampled 900 Hz tone appears at 300 Hz.

evidence_choices.label: Nyquist is 600 Hz and |900 - 1200| = 300 Hz
evidence_choices.reason: This directly connects undersampling to the observed peak.

evidence_choices.label: The FFT contains many bins
evidence_choices.reason: Bin count does not explain this frequency fold.

evidence_choices.label: The sensor amplitude is stable
evidence_choices.reason: Amplitude stability does not prove the analog frequency.

correction.template: Because Nyquist is {nyquist} Hz, the 900 Hz input aliases to {alias} Hz; the 300 Hz peak alone is not evidence of a separate tone.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Preserve the 900 Hz component without aliasing
gates.constraint: The 900 Hz component must remain measurable.

options.label: Increase the sample rate to 2400 samples/s
options.reason: Nyquist becomes 1200 Hz, above the 900 Hz signal.

options.label: Keep 1200 samples/s and trust the FFT
Reduce the sample rate to 1000 samples/s
Low-pass below 600 Hz while still requiring the 900 Hz component
options.reason: That removes the signal of interest.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the alias rule
gates.prompt: A 700 Hz tone is sampled at 1000 samples/s. What alias appears in the 0–500 Hz baseband?

options.label: 200 Hz
options.reason: The nearest multiple of fs gives 300 Hz.

options.label: 0 Hz
options.reason: It does not alias to DC.

gates.explanation: Frequencies above Nyquist fold into the baseband.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the sampling analysis
gates.confirmation: I confirm that sampled spectral peaks must be interpreted only after verifying the Nyquist condition or anti-alias filtering.

items.label: What appeared
items.value: A 300 Hz FFT peak appeared from a 900 Hz analog input.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The 900 Hz input exceeded the 600 Hz Nyquist frequency.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Check fs/2 before interpreting spectra; undersampled tones fold into baseband.

seo.seo_title: Aliasing and Nyquist: Why 900 Hz Looks Like 300 Hz | FE E-023
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Case E-023: a 900 Hz vibration sampled at 1200 Hz appears at 300 Hz. Diagnose aliasing, apply Nyquist, and fix the sample rate.
seo.excerpt: A 900 Hz vibration can look like a clean 300 Hz signal when the ADC samples too slowly.
seo.direct_answer: With a 1200 samples/s rate, the Nyquist frequency is 600 Hz. A 900 Hz input exceeds Nyquist and aliases to |900 - 1200| = 300 Hz, so the sampled spectrum can show a convincing 300 Hz peak that is not a separate analog vibration.

faqs.q: What is the Nyquist frequency for 1200 samples/s?
What does a 900 Hz tone alias to at 1200 samples/s?

faqs.a: Sample fast enough for the highest signal of interest and use appropriate anti-alias filtering before the ADC.
